precepts.text: Sow bountifully and reap bountifully; give as you purpose in your heart, not grudgingly or of necessity, for God loveth a cheerful giver.
precepts.point: He which soweth sparingly shall reap sparingly, and he which soweth bountifully shall reap bountifully; that does not mean the Most High blesses you with a three story house, for you may be storing up treasures in heaven. Give as you purpose in your heart, not grudgingly or of necessity, for God loveth a cheerful giver; giving with an attitude is worse than keeping the money.

note.label: Exodus 38: The Altar, the Court, and the Sum of the Offering

precepts.why:
“He which soweth sparingly shall reap also sparingly; and he which soweth bountifully shall reap also bountifully.” That does not mean the Most High blesses you with a three story house; you may be storing up treasures in heaven.

“Every man according as he purposeth in his heart, so let him give; not grudgingly, or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver.” As in the wilderness, when thousands of men gave their half shekels for the sanctuary, and as in Babylon, when our fathers made a collection according to every man's power, you give according to your power and as you purpose in your heart. Giving with an attitude is worse than keeping the money. Many do not have the spirit to give; if you have trouble coming up out of your pocket for the cause of the Lord, examine yourself whether ye be in the faith.

precepts.text: He which soweth sparingly shall reap also sparingly; and he which soweth bountifully shall reap also bountifully.
precepts.point: The rich cast in much, but the poor widow threw in two mites, and he says she cast in more than they all, for they cast in of their abundance, but she of her want did cast in all that she had.

note.label: Mark 12: The Husbandmen, the Tribute, and the First Commandment

precepts.why:
The rich cast much into the treasury, and a poor widow threw in two mites. “Verily I say unto you, That this poor widow hath cast more in, than all they which have cast into the treasury: For all they did cast in of their abundance; but she of her want did cast in all that she had, even all her living.”

Paul lays down the rule: “He which soweth sparingly shall reap also sparingly; and he which soweth bountifully shall reap also bountifully.” The rich gave much and sowed sparingly, because it was out of their abundance; the widow gave two mites and sowed bountifully, because it was all she had. The measure is not the sum but what it cost the giver, and the reaping follows that.
